text:
After 808 games in Columbus, Boone Jenner is a Washington Capital, and the change has suited his shot. He has 7 goals in 20 games while playing about 15.7 minutes a night, none of them on the power play. One of them carried a bit of history: Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted that Alex Ovechkin's assist on a Jenner goal was the 763rd of his career, passing Nicklas Backstrom's Capitals record.

The goals run ahead of the chances. His expected goals (the quality of his shots) come to 5.0, and he is shooting 16.3%, above the top of our range for him, so some cooling would be normal. The assists have been scarce, 2 all season, which keeps his scoring rate below his own norm.

He is a checking-line forward who kills penalties and plays a dump-and-chase game: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 25% of his entries last season, with 62% of his shots coming off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play (89th percentile among forwards). Our range for his season is 33 to 53 points.
